# Land of Stone Flowers
> Illustrated book by Sveta Dorosheva. Published by Chronicle Books (USA), Азбука (RU), マール社 (JP). 216 pages, hardcover, published in 7 languages.

## About
"The Land of Stone Flowers: A Fairy Guide to the Mythical Human Being" is an illustrated book written and illustrated by Ukrainian-Israeli artist Sveta Dorosheva. It was originally published in Russian as «Книга, найденная в кувшинке» (The Nenufar Book) by Издательство Азбука in 2016.

The book is a collection of illustrated fables told from the perspective of fairy-folk — gnomes, pixies, trolls and other magical beings from the Glimmering Land of Maar — who do not believe humans exist, and who report on human anatomy, customs, languages, rituals and dwellings with curiosity, wild speculation and dry wit. Recurring motifs include the paper wizards living in human wallets and the invisible hats known as "moods".

Every page is hand-drawn. The visual style is dense, ornamental folk art, frequently compared to Aubrey Beardsley and to fin-de-siecle illustrators such as Kay Nielsen, Edmund Dulac and George Barbier. Suitable for adults and older children.

## Key facts
- Author and illustrator: Sveta Dorosheva (she wrote and illustrated the book)
- Original language: Russian (2016)
- Pages: 216, hardcover, colour illustrations throughout
- Published in 7 languages
- Website: https://landofstoneflowers.com (EN / RU / JA)
